questions.prompt: You need the Biosig plugin to read an EDF file. Where do you install it inside EEGLAB?
questions.explanation: The extension manager is in the File menu: search for Biosig and click `Install/Update`; it needs an internet connection. `Edit > Preferences` holds EEGLAB options, not plugins.

questions.prompt: This is the main window after opening `eeglab_data.set`. What does it mean that `Epochs` is 1 here?

image.alt: The EEGLAB main window with the dataset name Continuous EEG Data at the top, and under it the value lines: Channels per frame, Frames per epoch, Epochs, Events, Sampling rate (Hz), Epoch start (sec), Epoch end (sec), Reference, Channel locations, ICA weights.
image.spec: A real EEGLAB 2026.1 screenshot (source: eeglab-ui) of the main window after opening eeglab_data.set, like the "after" image in the eeglab-gui lesson but **with no numbers or arrows** on top. Expected values: 32, 30504, 1, 154, 128, 0.000 and 238.305. The interface text is English, so one version serves both languages.

options.text: The data are continuous and have not been epoched yet
The dataset has only one channel
The dataset has only one event
The recording is one second long

questions.explanation: `Epochs` is the number of segments, and 1 means one continuous recording that has not been cut. The channel count is on the `Channels per frame` line, the event count on the `Events` line, and the length on the `Epoch end (sec)` line.

questions.prompt: The command `size(EEG.data)` prints `32 30504`. What do the two numbers mean?
questions.explanation: In EEGLAB channels are rows and samples are columns. So `EEG.data(1, :)` is the whole first channel, and `EEG.data(:, 1)` is all channels at the first sample.

questions.prompt: Which statements about the fields of `EEG` are true? (Select all that apply)

options.text: `EEG.srate` is the sampling rate in Hz
`EEG.event(1).latency` is the event time in samples, not seconds
`EEG.icaweights` is always filled after opening any dataset

questions.explanation: `EEG.times` is in milliseconds, while `EEG.xmin` and `EEG.xmax` are in seconds. `EEG.icaweights` stays empty until you compute ICA in station 4. To convert a latency to seconds: (sample number − 1) ÷ sampling rate.

questions.prompt: In the main window: `Frames per epoch` = 30504, `Sampling rate (Hz)` = 128, and `Epochs` = 1. About how long is the recording?
questions.explanation: `Frames per epoch` is a sample count, not seconds. Divide it by the sampling rate: 30504 ÷ 128 ≈ 238 seconds, roughly the number on the `Epoch end (sec)` line.
